source.title: A comparison of abstract rules in the prefrontal cortex, premotor cortex, inferior temporal cortex, and striatum.

confidence_rationale: Included for the subject-level grounding SD-082's architecture doc explicitly rests on -- 'corticostriatal rule-to-action mapping: a selected rule/context representation must gate a motor bias for the selection to have behavioural consequence; selection without a trained read-out to action is inert.' Muhammad et al. recorded across four connected areas while monkeys applied abstract 'same'/'different' rules to a hold-or-release response, and found rule information and response information co-represented in lateral PFC, premotor cortex and dorsal striatum, with negligible rule coding in inferior temporal cortex. That is direct primate evidence that abstract rule signals reach the structures that select actions rather than remaining confined to a rule-representing area -- the premise that makes SD-082's read-out a necessary component rather than an optional one, and that makes V3-EXQ-822's structural zero a genuine architectural defect rather than an acceptable design. But the paper also complicates SD-082's assumed direction of flow, and that is why the direction is mixed rather than supports: rules and behavioural responses 'were reflected most strongly and, on average, tended to be earlier in the PMC followed by the PFC and then the STR'. Premotor cortex leading prefrontal cortex is the opposite of the serial PFC-computes-rule-then-biases-action architecture that SD-082's data flow diagram encodes. Confidence 0.58: solid primate electrophysiology at the level of area-wise information content, but it evidences the EXISTENCE and DISTRIBUTION of a rule-to-action pathway, not the FORM of any read-out, and it says nothing at all about common-mode geometry or output bounds -- the two things SD-082 actually changes.
failure_signatures: DIRECTIONALITY. Rule and response signals appeared earliest and most strongly in PREMOTOR cortex, then PFC, then striatum. SD-082's data-flow diagram is strictly serial and prefrontal-first: CandidateRuleField -> rule_state -> LateralPFCAnalog.compute_bias -> E3 per-candidate score_bias. If the biology is closer to concurrent or premotor-led rule/action coding, then SD-082 correctly identifies that a read-out must exist while getting its architectural placement wrong, and no amount of tuning at the LateralPFCAnalog read-out would reproduce the biological computation. This is not a defect that V3-EXQ-822a can detect -- 822a tests whether propagation is non-vacuous, which a wrongly-placed-but-functional read-out would pass.

The paper resolves rule and response coding at the level of area-wise information content and latency, with no measurement of the geometry of the population code and no test of how a downstream area reads it. It therefore cannot discriminate between ANY of the candidate read-out mechanisms SD-082 chose among -- raw versus centered input, hard clamp versus scaled tanh are all equally consistent with these data. Citing it as support for SD-082's mechanism (as opposed to SD-082's necessity) would be an overreach.

The task uses two abstract rules ('same'/'different') and a binary hold-or-release response, so the candidate set has cardinality two and there is no meaningful 'across-candidate mean' to speak of. SD-082's centering is gated on K >= 2 and its benefit is expected to grow with candidate-set size (V3-EXQ-822 had max_live 16 rules). This paradigm is at the extreme low end of that range and provides no evidence about the many-similar-alternatives regime that is precisely where the common-mode pathology bites.

Rule coding was negligible in inferior temporal cortex while perceptual identity information was strongest and earliest there -- a clean dissociation showing the rule pathway is selective, not a broadcast. If REE's rule_state is read by consumers that should NOT see it, this paper is a reason to check that selectivity; SD-082 adds a consumer without any stated gating on which downstream structures may read the rule signal.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Monkeys trained to apply two abstract rules ('same' or 'different') to a hold-or-release lever response showed rule and response information distributed across connected areas: rules and behavioural responses were reflected most strongly, and on average tended to be earlier, in premotor cortex, followed by lateral prefrontal cortex, then dorsal striatum, with few inferior temporal neurons reflecting rules or actions. Perceptual information about the pictures was encoded more strongly and earlier in inferior temporal cortex followed by PFC, with weak or absent effects in premotor cortex and striatum. Abstract rule use allows behaviour to generalise beyond specific circumstances.
mapping.ree_translation: This is the primate evidence behind SD-082's stated biological grounding: an abstract rule representation is only functional insofar as it reaches the structures that select actions, and in the biology it demonstrably does -- rule signals are co-represented with response signals in premotor cortex and striatum, not sequestered in a rule-representing prefrontal module. Applied to REE, it makes the V3-EXQ-822 finding (a differentiated rule pool, on_rule_state_diff_mean 0.644, with propagation to the action bias at exactly 0.0) a real architectural defect rather than a tolerable design choice: a rule field whose content never reaches action selection is not implementing the biology it is modelled on. That is the justification for SD-082 existing at all. It supplies no constraint on HOW the read-out should compute -- centering and the tanh bound are both invisible at this paper's resolution.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Load-bearing caveat: the LATENCY ORDERING runs against SD-082's architecture. Rule and response signals led in premotor cortex, then PFC, then striatum, whereas SD-082 encodes a strictly serial prefrontal-first flow (rule_state computed in the CandidateRuleField, read out by LateralPFCAnalog, then applied as an E3 score bias). The paper's ordering is consistent with concurrent or premotor-led rule/action coding, so SD-082 may be right that a read-out is required and wrong about where it sits. Secondary caveats: the paradigm has two rules and a binary response, i.e. the smallest candidate set in which centering is even defined, and it is furthest from the many-similar-alternatives regime where the common-mode pathology bites (822 had max_live 16); the measurements are area-wise information content and latency, with no population geometry and no read-out model, so the data cannot discriminate among SD-082's candidate mechanisms; and this is macaque single-unit physiology mapped onto a V3 lateral-PFC ANALOG whose correspondence to primate lateral PFC is architectural convention rather than a measured homology.
mapping.source_context: Primate electrophysiology. Macaques (Macaca mulatta) trained on a delayed match/non-match task under two cued abstract rules, requiring lever hold or release depending on whether successive pictures were the same or different and on which rule was in force. Single-unit recordings compared across lateral prefrontal cortex, premotor cortex, inferior temporal cortex and dorsal striatum, with ROC-based analysis of rule, response and perceptual information and of relative latency.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality 0.82: well-executed four-area comparison from the Miller lab, an established paradigm, ROC-quantified, peer-reviewed -- though a 2006 single-lab primate study with the usual small-n structure, and latency orderings across areas are notoriously sensitive to analysis choices, which matters here because a latency ordering is doing real work in the caveat. Mapping fidelity 0.45: the paper grounds SD-082's NECESSITY (a rule representation must reach action selection) and not its CONTENT (how the read-out computes), and SD-082 is a claim about the content -- its two components are a centering operation and an output bound, neither of which this paradigm could see. Transfer risk 0.50: macaque physiology to a V3 lateral-PFC analog, and a two-rule binary-response task to a 16-rule pool with per-candidate biases. Aggregate 0.58, direction mixed: it substantiates the claim that a silent rule pool is a defect worth fixing -- which is the load SD-082's architecture doc asks it to carry -- while its latency ordering is a standing question about whether SD-082's serial prefrontal-first placement is the right one, a question V3-EXQ-822a is not designed to answer.
